A baby demon is born in Nekravol and learns how to walk, talk, and think from his demon parents. Years and years of growing up shape this young demon into a very academic, truly prosperous demon citizen. His parents cried at his graduation, and are always in awe of how much this demon child can get done. It is truly a thing of beauty.

But then he was drafted for the war.

DOOM Eternal feels like finding a bowl of your favorite candy that has been laced with pure human adrenaline. The pace feels great, the controls feel smooth and responsive, and the game-play loop is so very satisfying when it finally clicked in my ADHD riddled mind. It felt strange at first but before long I was jumping around arenas, juggling weapons and abilities and mowing down an onslaught of demons that use everything they have to bring me down.

Managing rescores by using certain attacks feels amazing and constantly awards you with hits of dopamine. Need ammo? Chainsaw time. Need health? glory kill away. Then setting some demons on fire so they drop armor and on top of that each demon has a weakness to exploit when you aren't trying to regain lost health or ammo. It just plain feels good.

The story is pretty good too, though purposely campy, placing a greater emphasis on the series' lore than previous entries, exploring the Slayer's origins and the mythology surrounding his endless hatred for the demons, while maintaining the fast-paced action that define the franchise.

Well it's Doom and I'm a Doom fan and player since the early 90's. Game looks gorgeous, it's fast and gory as you'd expect. Requires a lot of skill to really dominate it in harder difficulties. Surely they've been successful on their choices for Doom 2016 and Eternal, and there is a much anticipated Doom The Dark Ages coming in a couple of months, but I'm just not sure if I really like the path they are taking the theme of the franchise focusing on more mythological/ancient/medieval settings. Recommend it for sure especially to fans.

At first I didn't really like the changes from DOOM 2016. The fact that the game became more about resource management, rather than simply optimizing targets. I also didn't care for the addition of the Marauders. It seemed to slow the game down and the kit that this enemy had was too good in my opinion, resulting in some very frustrating deaths.

But, the more and more I played, I began to enjoy the arsenal you are supplied to get all the things you need. As well as the weak point system was a great addition in regards to the lack of ammo. The level design was great for pretty much every level of the game.

Overall, it's a very fun and challenging game, that still has the fast paced killing and gun play.

9/10

I loved Doom 2016, it was a great game that, in my opinion, didn't need much to improve. If anything, it could use some fat-trimming. Eternal does none of that, it doubles down on mind-numbingly boring stuff like collectathons and pseudo-rpg progressions. But the showstopper for me was the pole-swinging monkey sections, some of which are mandatory to progress the game. I don't mind spatial puzzles, but platforming sections in FPP games have always sucked and alienated audiences, and it's no exception here.

tldr.text: Very Positive (91%): players love the combat, the story and the music.
The most common complaint is also the combat, where some feel the balance is off.

details.text: Players in their first hours are 58% positive, while those with long playtimes are 96% positive, so new buyers may not feel the same pull at first.
Recent reviews are less positive overall, mention bugs less often, and complain more about difficulty, with one reviewer calling it "artificial difficulty".
